letter.subject: Concern regarding cookie and tracking practices on natwestgroup.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified on https://natwestgroup.com during an automated, passive privacy audit carried out on 2026-11-08 04:08 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit detected the cookie banner, clicked “Reject Non-Essential Cookies”, and recorded what was still sent while browsing continued.

The pages visited after rejection were:
1. https://www.natwestgroup.com/who-we-are.html
2. https://www.natwestgroup.com/who-we-are/board-and-governance.html
3. https://www.natwestgroup.com/sustainability.html

I also reviewed your cookie/privacy information at https://www.natwestgroup.com/cookie-privacy.html.

The issues I ask you to explain are as follows:
1. Our review suggests YouTube advertising loaded without valid consent. A YouTube advertising request was recorded before the banner was answered and another was recorded after the user clicked “Reject Non-Essential Cookies”. This appears difficult to reconcile with your policy statement: “Some cookies can impact your fundamental rights to privacy and the protection of your data. As such, we require your consent before they can be accessed or stored on your device.”
2. Google still received data after cookies were rejected. We observed 1 request to youtube.com after “Reject Non-Essential Cookies” was clicked, categorised as advertising.
3. Adobe still received data after cookies were rejected. We observed 66 requests to adobedtm.com after rejection, categorised as analytics. I appreciate that some audience-measurement analytics may be exempt, but this would need clear justification.
4. Our review suggests a transparency issue in relation to recipients named in the policy. The policy names 4 companies. We observed Adobe and found no mention of Adobe by name, although it is possible the policy refers to it only by category.

Please:
1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies or trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking that occurs without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter cannot be resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
